memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He set the altar of burnt offering near the entrance to the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, and offered on it burnt offerings and grain offerings, as the Lord commanded him." - Exod 40:29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The altar stood where everyone would meet it first — at the entrance. And the moment it was in place, Moses used it.

There is no delay here. The tabernacle was not a museum piece to admire. Within moments of assembly, sacrifices were burning.

Notice the two offerings named. The burnt offering was consumed entirely — nothing held back, the whole animal given (Lev 1:9). The grain offering was from the produce of human labour, the fruit of ordinary work.

Together they say something. God asks for whole-hearted devotion and for the ordinary results of daily life. Not one or the other.

Paul draws on the same idea when he calls us to offer our bodies as living sacrifices (Rom 12:1), and when he describes gifts received from the Philippians as a fragrant offering, an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God (Phil 4:18).

But hold this carefully. The daily sacrifices at that altar had to be repeated endlessly because they could never take away sins (Heb 10:11). Their whole purpose was to point beyond themselves.

Christ offered one sacrifice for sins for all time and then sat down (Heb 10:12). The altar could never be finished. He said, "It is finished."

We do not offer for sin. We offer in gratitude.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is your devotion whole or partial?
2. Do you offer God the fruit of your ordinary work?
3. Do you live as though the sacrifice for your sin is finished?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You offered Yourself once for all. I bring You my whole life in thanks, not to pay a debt You have settled. Amen.
